issues.description: docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-028.md's AC1 fixture narrative names lastName values "A0".."A11" (unpadded) and asserts the attendee named "A10" lands at sorted index 10 (page 1). Verified this claim before building on it (per core-directives.md's 'a handoff's factual claims must be verified, not trusted'): under Postgres's default text ordering (byte/lexicographic, matching JS string comparison), unpadded "A0".."A11" actually sorts as A0, A1, A10, A11, A2, A3, ..., A9 -- "A10" lands at index 2 (page 0), not index 10, which would have silently exercised the wrong page. This run's implementation instead zero-pads to "A00".."A11" so lexicographic order matches numeric order, which is what the spec's own narrative intent (deterministic order, target attendee on page 1 at index 10) actually requires -- the scenario, assertions, and failure mode are otherwise implemented exactly as designed. Recommend TEST-DESIGNER correct the spec's own worked example (use zero-padded lastName values) on its next revision so a future implementer doesn't have to re-derive this.
